population.span: Eligible patients were at least 40 years old with a history of T2DM and established CV disease.

endpoint.span: time to first major adverse CV event (MACE, the composite of CV death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke)

estimate.span: The primary MACE outcome occurred in 114/2092 patients in the omarigliptin group (5.45%; 2.96/100 patient-years) and 114/2100 patients in the placebo group (5.43%; 2.97/100 patient-years), with a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77, 1.29).

ci.span: The primary MACE outcome occurred in 114/2092 patients in the omarigliptin group (5.45%; 2.96/100 patient-years) and 114/2100 patients in the placebo group (5.43%; 2.97/100 patient-years), with a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77, 1.29).

analysis_set.span: The population analyzed was the ITT population that included all randomized patients who took at least 1 dose of blinded study medication and all CV endpoint data, regardless of the time since a patient may have discontinued blinded study medication.

treatment_strategy.span: In this randomized, double-blind study, 4202 patients with T2DM and established CV disease were assigned to either omarigliptin 25 mg q.w. or matching placebo in addition to their existing diabetes therapy.

follow_up.span: The median follow-up was approximately 96 weeks (range 1.1–178.6 weeks).

served_mismatch: The served HR and CI match. The source calls the analysis ITT but restricts it to randomized patients who received at least one dose. The served timepoint 'trial end' requires qualification: results use the May 13, 2016 data cutoff, when some patients remained in follow-up; subsequent CV events were excluded.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Adults with T2DM and established cardiovascular disease fall within the question's adult T2DM population.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Eligible patients were at least 40 years old with a history of T2DM and established CV disease.

notes: All bindings use the held full text. The trial terminated early; the numerical candidate is retained. The source-defined ITT population excludes randomized patients who never received study medication.
